items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1961-01-20
items.q: I got my inspiration from Henry Martin, Black Benny, Red Happy, Baby Dodds.

ctx.x: And, well, he got his inspiration from Bunk. And I got my inspiration from Henry Martin, Black Benny, Red Happy, Baby Dodds. But Baby Dodds used to play in the Orleans during them times. Yeah. Well, after I got old enough I used to go to dances. I, wherever Baby Dodds was playing I was always there. And actually I got a lot from, learned a lot from him. Oh, sure. Yeah. Well, when I, around 1918, I was taking press roll lessons from Henry Martin. Yeah. He was a left-hander like me.

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: And I used to watch Baby Dots anytime when I got a chance to go hear them, and I used to watch Henry Martin, I watched Black Benny, and Red Happy, and all those fellas that was making a name for themselves.

ctx.x: And I used to watch Baby Dots anytime when I got a chance to go hear them, and I used to watch Henry Martin, I watched Black Benny, and Red Happy, and all those fellas that was making a name for themselves. And, well I never did learn music, I just taken interest, so much interest in it that I fell in love with the drums and I'd taken them up.
When you were a kid, did you play on any toy drums or beat on anything?

items.title: Joe Watkins Interview, 1960-03-16
items.q: I copied that from Happi because Happi used to do that really.

ctx.x: Well that's, I copied that from Happi because Happi used to do that really. Happi used to do that all the time, you know. And, well he wanted to go to a dance. He even went and rented the snare drum so he could get in the dance without paying, you know, because he was charging admission at the door. Well he carried the snare drum along with him and this letter went right on. He just went up on the bandstand and get up there and set the drum up a while, you know, rest him up and, well I started doing the same…
Well I can ask more about Joe Lynch's.
